name: Compatible time sharing with persistent files and batch service
summary: By 1963 MIT's Compatible Time-Sharing System let many people use one IBM 7090 at once through terminals, keep named files on disk, and leave batch work running.
description: A 1963 CTSS configuration combining interactive shared access, named persistent disk files, supervisor protection and compatibility with a batch-processing service on an IBM 7090.
tier_reason: The scoped record is a particular configuration, local witness, trial or material application. Dependence across fields or generations on THIS referent is not established; do not inherit the importance of its broader missing family.

date.label: by 1963-08
date.basis: Latest supported use or availability; the first worldwide entry is not established.

events.statement: Visitors at the 1963 Project MAC Summer Study used CTSS through terminals by August 1963 while the host computer continued batch work.
events.scope: 1963 MIT CTSS service, accessed through terminals while the 7090 continued FMS batch service.
applications: Interactive programming and shared computational research
events.population: Project MAC summer-study visitors from universities, industry and government
events.caveats: The 1961 CTSS demonstration is earlier but does not establish all 1963 service features. BBN already operated protected time sharing from 1962. The sources do not establish that each summer visitor personally used every disk-file feature or that CTSS was the first file service. Access through terminals did not imply ownership of the central computer.

evidence.supports: A participant history describes visitors using CTSS via terminals while FMS batch work continued.
The 1963 guide describes protected operation and named disk files.
A participant retrospective connects the upgraded disk-based hardware configuration to summer 1963.
BBN had already operated a protected PDP-1 time-sharing system.
The 1963 authors report BBN service from September 1962 and identify the absence of a drum program library.

date.basis: Publication year of the cited document, not necessarily the first use of the described arrangement.

events.statement: The 1963 CTSS guide describes login using problem and programmer numbers, accounting at logout, and restrictions on referencing unauthorized files.

evidence.supports: The guide describes user problem and programmer numbers at login, per-session accounting at logout, and authorization boundaries on disk-file references. It discusses a private code as a future possibility rather than asserting it was already required.

events.caveats: The guide describes a private code as a future possibility; it does not establish passwords were already required, how users obtained eligibility, or a price.
